# Origin Isolation Checklist: Cluster Frames

**Purpose**: Check that the requirements on keeping each cluster frame apart in WKWebView are complete, clear, consistent and measurable before tasks are written.
**Created**: 2026-11-25
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md), with [plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md) and [contracts/](../contracts/)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Does the spec require isolation in both directions, the main window kept from a cluster frame's document and page state as well as a frame from the main window's? [Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements defined for a cluster frame navigating the main window or another frame (setting its location), as opposed to reading or changing its document? [Gap, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for what a cluster frame may open outside itself, such as a new window or a popup, and which origin and capabilities that window gets? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK004 Does the spec state whether cross-origin `postMessage` between frames, and between a frame and the main window, is an allowed path or outside the isolation guarantee? [Gap, Spec §US1]
- [ ] CHK005 Does the spec state which page may embed a cluster frame, so that a cluster's origin cannot be framed by another cluster's page? [Gap, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK006 Are the browser permissions a cluster frame gets (clipboard, which the Electron build grants its frames, and any other) specified for the Tauri build? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK007 Does the spec say what network access content in a cluster frame has outside the scheme, such as loading or sending to an external address? [Gap]
- [ ] CHK008 Is it required that a hidden frame stays recorded for as long as it is open, so that hiding a frame cannot make the core forget it and drop its messages? [Gap, Spec §FR-010, §FR-012]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK009 Is "browser storage" enumerated precisely enough to test: local and session storage, databases and caches are named, but are service workers and their caches in or out? [Clarity, Spec §Definitions, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK010 Does FR-004 say whether a cookie a view sets may stay visible within that same view, or only that no other view sees it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004]
- [ ] CHK011 Is "from where its request comes from" defined as the request's host and origin, so that a request with no `Origin` header still has one defined identity? [Clarity, Spec §FR-008]
- [ ] CHK012 Is "refused" in FR-007 given an observable form, and is it consistent with FR-005's "no content" for unknown hosts? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK013 Is "page state" defined so that a reviewer can tell it apart from browser storage when judging FR-013, which keeps one and not the other on reopen? [Clarity, Spec §Definitions, §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK014 Is "the same origin across restarts" distinguished from "the same storage across restarts", given that the plan keeps a website data store that does not outlive a run? [Clarity, Spec §FR-001, Plan R2]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK015 Does the narrative of User Story 1, "a request for one cluster's data from another cluster's frame is refused", agree with the assumption that every channel stays open to every view and answers for the cluster it names? [Conflict, Spec §US1, §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 Does the definition of closing a cluster (disconnecting it, or removing it from the catalog) match the Close of the catalog page, which removes the frame and does neither? [Conflict, Spec §Definitions, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK017 Is the 60-second bound measured from the same moment in FR-012 ("after the frame stops listening") and in SC-005 ("after the close")? [Consistency, Spec §FR-012, §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK018 Is "as in the Electron build" for storage across restarts consistent with a Tauri data store that does not persist, while the Electron build's does? [Consistency, Spec §Edge Cases, Plan R2]
- [ ] CHK019 Are the route answers of the spec (refused, no content) consistent with the order of checks and the status codes of `contracts/routes.md`, including a foreign `Origin` on an unknown path? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005 to §FR-007]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK020 Does SC-002 list every attempt FR-002 to FR-007 forbid, including changing another frame's document, a main-window-only route, and the two channels with sender checks, or only reading? [Coverage, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK021 Does SC-002 name which kinds of browser storage the check must cover, so that passing with `localStorage` alone is not taken as covering databases and caches? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK022 Can SC-003's "neither of them reloads" be decided from a recorded value rather than by watching the screen? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]
- [ ] CHK023 Is the pass condition of SC-004 explicit that the reopened frame's browser storage is kept while its page state is new? [Clarity, Spec §SC-004, §FR-013]

## Scenario and Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK024 Are requirements defined for a cluster that leaves the catalog while its frame is open, given that the Tauri catalog does not change during a run in this feature? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK025 Are hosts that differ only by letter case, a trailing dot or a port covered by FR-005, so that one cluster cannot have two origins? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-001, §FR-005]
- [ ] CHK026 Is the reload of a single cluster frame covered for isolation as well as for the record: does the reloaded frame keep its origin and storage and lose its page state? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK027 Is a crash or hang of one frame's content addressed in the requirements, or explicitly excluded in a way consistent with "closing one does not affect the others"? [Coverage, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-011]

## Non-Functional Requirements

- [ ] CHK028 Does the spec state whether the cluster's origin may reveal anything about the kubeconfig, such as its path or context name, given that the id is derived from both? [Gap, Security, Spec §FR-001]
- [ ] CHK029 Is the data that broadcast channels deliver to every frame, such as another cluster's state, acknowledged as outside the isolation guarantee, and is that stated where the guarantee is? [Assumption, Spec §US1, §Assumptions]

## Dependencies and Assumptions

- [ ] CHK030 Is the dependency on WebKit to refuse cross-origin reads and requests stated as an assumption, with the core's checks named as the second line, so that a reviewer knows which part the core guarantees? [Assumption, Spec §FR-006, Research R2]
- [ ] CHK031 Is the assumption that the rules hold for the pages a later spec serves, "because they are rules of the origin and the core", backed by a requirement that later pages add no route or channel outside those rules? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions, §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK032 Are the facts the isolation relies on that are still unverified (WebKit's handling of a hidden frame, removing a frame without blanking it, cookies on the scheme) listed with how the feature learns them? [Assumption, Research R2, R11]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Scope: isolation between the views of the Tauri build on WKWebView, as the spec, the plan and the contracts state it. The removal of `request-freelens-proxy-certificate` and the parity of the Electron build are out of this checklist except where they bear on isolation.
- Depth: standard, as a review gate before `/speckit-tasks`. Audience: the reviewer of the spec and plan.
- CHK015 and CHK016 look like conflicts in the spec as written; the others are gaps or points to make precise.
- Changes made in answer to the items, for the reviewer to judge; no marker was set:

  - plan: research R3 (hosts with a port or a user name), R7, R9 (the attempts of SC-002), new R12 (navigation, windows, framing, permissions, outside addresses), R11 (the sandbox as a risk); `contracts/routes.md`, `contracts/frames-log.md`, `plan.md` and `quickstart.md` to match.
